purpose: CPU-only sample-budget diagnostic: does the same CA lDDT medoid benefit enough from nine predictions to justify additional generation cost?
status: Frozen before nine-sample choices or their native scores are computed
checkpoint: Untouched final EMA pair; same strict FP32 head/decoder, 25 steps, CFG 2, and all 626 development proteins
selector: Concatenate samples 0,1,2 from the three runs in the stated order. Choose the sample with largest average symmetric CA lDDT to the other eight. Keep existing 15 A neighborhoods and strict 0.5/1/2/4 A error thresholds; first index wins exact ties. No native input or fitted coefficients.
freeze: Validate matching checkpoint, decoder, data, precision and coverage; hash protocol, manifests, predictions and prior three-sample choices. Write nine-sample choices before opening any native score file. Verify the generic implementation reproduces every previously frozen three-sample choice.
primary_comparison: Selected nine-sample TM versus the per-target mean performance of the three existing three-sample medoids. The latter estimates a three-sample selector's expectation over these noise groups; it does not average coordinates.
secondary_comparison: Selected nine versus the nine-sample mean (random-sample expectation), with CA lDDT and geometry fractions reported. Native-TM best-of-nine is an oracle upper bound only.
uncertainty: Paired sequence-cluster bootstrap; samples are repeated measurements. This pools previously examined noise groups and reused targets, so any benefit is exploratory.
followup_gate: New GPU sampling only if selected TM reaches untouched mean plus 0.01, improves over three-sample medoid expectation by at least 0.003 with a positive 95% cluster lower bound, CA lDDT lower bound at least -0.005 and geometry upper bounds at most +0.001. Then repeat with a new nine-sample pool before any further decision.
cost: Zero new GPU generation for this diagnostic. Deployment needs nine generated structures per selected protein: three times the head/decoder sample budget of the three-sample rule. ESMC embeddings can be reused. Report existing generation times and measured CPU analysis time without claiming optimized deployment throughput.
final_test: Unscored; earlier-layer ESM GPU budget remains zero
